title: O₂: 32 g to moles
hook: Turn a sample mass into an amount of substance.

knows: A mole counts an amount of substance.
doesNotKnow: How mass and molar mass determine moles.

misconception: A gram is the same amount in moles for every substance.
objective: Convert an indicated mass to moles using a supplied molar mass.

claims.text: A sample of O₂ has a mass of 32 g. Using its rounded molar mass of 32 g/mol, how many moles are present? Amount = mass ÷ molar mass = 32 g ÷ 32 g/mol = 1 mol.
claims.source: Arithmetic using supplied rounded molar mass; OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/3-1-formula-mass-and-the-mole-concept

claims.text: The sample diagram is schematic and is not a picture of individual particles.
Recall: For a fixed substance, if sample mass doubles, what happens to its amount in moles? The molar mass stays fixed, so moles = mass ÷ molar mass.
The supplied molar mass converts grams of this particular substance to moles; a different substance can have a different conversion factor.
claims.source: Arithmetic using supplied rounded molar mass; OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/3-1-formula-mass-and-the-mole-concept
